# Test fixtures

**`mysql-auto-generated-ca.pem`** — a throwaway MySQL 8.4 auto-generated CA, used by
`test_reconciler_mysql.py` to exercise `tls_context`.

It is here, and not read from `deploy/inference/kustomize/base/reconciler/`, because a test that
reads a `deploy/**` artifact couples the code suite to the deploy tree — and this repo splits
those into separate pushes. CI then checks out an intermediate commit that has the code and not
the manifest, and 22 tests fail with `FileNotFoundError` on a tree that is green everywhere else.
That happened on 2026-10-11 (run 38154300627); the merged branch passed locally and on `main`,
because the intermediate state a split push creates is tested by nothing except CI.

It is a real certificate rather than a stub because `ssl.create_default_context(cafile=...)`
parses it, and the properties under test are properties of this exact *shape*: self-signed, and
carrying no `authorityKeyIdentifier`, which is what Python 3.13's `VERIFY_X509_STRICT` rejects.
Generated by a `mysql:8.4` container that no longer exists, so it secures nothing — the server's
real CA is the one in `deploy/`, and a separate test checks that it is still valid.
